programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: When a penguin takes a shine to Stink's bed, and Grumblestunk decides to open a zoo, Brody is unimpressed, so Stan and Gran are forced to investigate! Nuair a tha ceann-fionn a' gabhail nòisean den leabaidh aig Samh, 's tha Greannarlobht a' cur roimhpe sù fhosgladh, chan eil Murchadh air a dhòigh, 's le sin, chan eil roghainn aig Dan is Gran ach teannadh ri rannsachadh!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Nuair a lorgas Sif, Pipp agus Bran sreang-fhiacaill, tha farpais tarraing ròpa air fàire! Ziff, Pipp and Button discover dental floss and plan an exciting tug-of-war showdown!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Meanbh Chlangair 's a caraidean Lusach, a' cluich ceòl còmhla ris na Craobhan Ciùil. Dè tha siud? Tha cuideigin eile ri seinn cuideachd. Saoil cò th' ann? Tiny Clanger and her flower friends are making music with the Music Trees. What’s that? Someone else is singing, too. Who could it be?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha a’ Chearc Iarainn an-dòchas gum bi cuideigin ann a ghabhas a cuid sgudail. Saoil ciamar a thèid dhi? The Iron Chicken is hopeful that she will find someone who will take her rubbish. How will she get on?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Teàrlach a’ faireachdainn tinn is chan eil e airson cluich. Tha Peicein agus a charaidean a’ feuchainn ri bruidhinn ris, tha iad a’ teagasg an cànan fhèin dha, is a’ feuchainn ri cainnt nan con ionnsachadh iad fhèin. Tadeo is feeling sick and doesn't want to play. Petit and his friends try to communicate with him, teaching Tadeo human language and trying to learn dog talk themselves.

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha an t-Iasg-èibhinn ag innse dhuinn gum bi iad a' fuireach air bun-dùn, mar a bhios iad a’ cumail a' bhun-dhùin glan agus mar a bhios am bun-dùn dhan cumail sàbhailte. The Clownfish tells us how they live on sea anemone which they keep clean, and how anemone in turn keep Clownfish safe from predators.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Dòmhnall Ruadh a’ leughadh Beatha Dhìomhair Tìgeir. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Emilia Dziubak agus a dhealbhachadh le Przemyslaw Wechterowicz. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Donald Smith reads Beatha Dhìomhair Tìgeir by Emilia Dziubak, illustrated by Przemyslaw Wechterowicz and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair tha Camshron a' tighinn tarsainn air ugh iolair-dhubh, tha e airson an t-ugh a chumail dha fhèin. Tha e cho rag. Ciamar a gheibh na seòid air an ugh a thilleadh don nead 's a chumail sàbhailt’? When Cameron comes across a black eagle’s egg, he wants to keep the egg for himself - he is so stubborn! How will the gang manage to return the egg to the nest and keep it safe?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach a' co-dhùnadh gu bheil an t-àm ann fàs fallain - agus tha e ag iarraidh Bitzer a thoirt a-steach air cùisean. Tha beachd eile aig Bitzer ge-tà agus tha e a' tighinn an àrd le plana dìomhair gus an obair chruaidh a sheachnadh. An dèan an sgeama aige a' chùis aig a' cheann thall? The farmer decides it is time to get fit and calls on Bitzer to join him. Bitzer has other ideas and comes up with a secret plan to avoid putting in the hard work. Will his scheme catch up with him in the end?

programme.title: Aidan: Balach Beag Muay Thai
programme.desc: Tha Aidan ag ullachachadh airson sabaid mhòr aig Farpais Muay Thai na Cruinne. Aidan prepares to compete in the biggest Muay Thai fight of his life.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Nuair a bha an t-eagal air Tabaidh bhon t-sluagh, tha a caraidean airson a cuideachadh agus misneachd a thoirt dhi, gus am faigh i air seinn aig an t-seoth' tàlant. When Tabaidh gets stage fright, her friends want to help and give her confidence, so that she can perform at the talent show.

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo seallaidh i dhut dòigh sgoinneil air coltas eadar-dhealaichte a thoirt air do chuid aodaich! Choirstaidh presents from her studio A’ Chùil to show you a great way of changing up your clothes.

programme.title: Golf: Mun Cuairt Alba
programme.desc: Featuring the story of golf at Askernish in South Uist, while professional coach Keil Beveridge gives us his weekly top playing tip.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre gar toirt tro thuilleadh cheumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Joy Dunlop continues to guide us through further steps to speak Gaelic.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets singer Mary Ann Kennedy in Ardgour. Although born in Glasgow, Mary Ann discusses how she has made her home in Ardgour and what that means to her. As they walk along Cona Glen, Mary Ann opens up about feeling comfortable in her own skin and how the environment has helped her find peace. She chats about her changing relationship with music and what brings her happiness. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri Màiri Anna NicUalraig ann an Àird Ghobhar. Ged a rugadh i ann an Glaschu, innsidh Mairi Anna an luach a tha i cuir air far a bheil i air a dachaigh a steidheachadh. A ’coiseachd tron Chona Ghleann, fuasglaidh Màiri Anna suas ma beachdan air a pearsa fhèin agus mar a tha an àrainneachd mu chuairt air a cuideachadh gus sìth a lorg. Tha conaltradh ann ma caochladh dhàimh le ceòl agus dè dìreach a tha toirt toileachas dhi. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc: Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus faighinn a-mach mun chrìoch eadar an Spàinn agus Moroco. Ann an Ceuta tha feansa àrd a’ sgaradh Afraga agus an Roinn Eòrpa agus dha mòran is e seo an geata chun na Roinn Eòrpa. Coinnichidh Ramsay ri imrichean a tha air a h-uile càil a tha aca a chuir ann an cunnart is iad a’ dol tarsainn air a’ bhalla an tòir air beatha nas fheàrr. Cluinnidh e bho luchd-còmhnaidh ionadail Ceuta a tha beò fo sgàil teannachadh poilitigeach agus coinnichidh e ri daoine a bhios ag obair gus an fheadhainn as motha a th’ ann an cunnart a chuideachadh. Ramsay MacMahon goes on a journey to find out about the border between Spain and Morocco. In Ceuta, a high fence separates Africa and Europe, and for many, this is the gateway to Europe. Ramsay meets migrants who have risked everything to cross the wall in the hope of a better life. He hears from local residents who live with the political tensions and meets people who work to help the most vulnerable. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Am buannaiche dhuaisean Calum McIlroy agus còmhlan-ciùil aig Duaisean nan Trads 2024. Anns an t-seata, Strathspeys & Reel, The Banks of Newfoundland agus Polonessa Spoof. Award-winning musician Calum McIlroy and band, recorded at the 2024 Trad Awards. The set includes Strathspeys & Reel, The Banks of Newfoundland and Polonessa Spoof.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: The mountain amphitheatre of Torridon is famed both for its spectacular winter environment and the rock climbing available in summer months. To gain a full understanding of this incredible area, Coinneach Rankin travels there at opposite ends of the year. With his partner Rori Hawthorn, the pair experience the full range of Scottish weather, access icy summits and enjoy picturesque cragging on an idyllic summer’s day. Tha cruth-tìre bheanntachail Thoirbheartan cliùiteach an dà chuid son a h-àrainneachd geamhrachail agus an sreap air creig a gheibhear ann as t-samhradh. Gus làn tuigse fhaotainn air an t- àite sònraichte seo, thèid Coinneach MacFhraing ann aig gach ceann den bhliadhna. Cuide ri a charaid Rori Hawthorn, cuiridh e eòlas air làn caochlaideachd aimsir na h-Alba, ruigidh e bearraidhean deigheach agus thèid e an sàs anns na creagan air latha brèagha ‘sa ghrèin. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc: In 2019, a catastrophic fire threatened Notre-Dame’s structure. Analysing the vaults of the building, researchers unveil its history and decipher the secrets of its past resistance.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le The Atholl Set ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform The Atholl Set in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: It’s make or break time at the Hebridean family-run tweed mill, ‘Muileann Mhicsuain’. Time is running out for mill owner Seumas as he tries to save his business, but his corner-cutting has horrific consequences. A dreadful accident takes place on the mill floor that endangers the life of a beloved employee, Old Mary. With the family business in jeopardy, Seumas makes a secret phone call asking for help, but who is he reaching out to and why does he have to keep it secret from his family? Tha taghaidhean mòra air thoiseach orra aig Muileann MhicSuain, a’ mhuileann chlò Innse Gall a th’ air a ruith le teaghlach MhicSuain. Tha an ùine a’ ruith air ceannard na muilne, Seumas, agus e a’ dèanamh nas urrainn dhà gus a’ ghnìomhachas aige a shàbhaileadh – ach tha cùisean a’ tighinn gu ceann uabhasach ri linn an dòigh-obrach charach aige. Tha tubaist eagalach a’ tachairt air làr na muilne a tha a’ cur beatha tè dhen luchd-obrach, Màiri, ann an cunnart. Le gnìomhachas an teaghlaich fo imcheist, tha Seumas a’ cur a dh’iarraidh cuideachadh – ach cò dhà a tha e a’ faighneachd agus carson a dh’fheumas e a chumail bhon chòrr dhen teaghlach? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bing is Sula a’ cluich còmhla ri Nicky, co-ogha Sula, tha speuclairean Nicky a' briseadh agus tha Sula is Bing a’ dol a mach air a chèile. When Bing and Sula play with Nicky, Sula’s cousin, Nicky breaks his glasses and Sula and Bing fall out.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Chan eil Teàrlaidh air a dhòigh nuair a tha e faicinn Bing dreiste mar ghreimear-a-saurus airson Oidhche Shamhna ach, aig a cheann thall, tha e tuigsinn gur e dìreach plòigh a th’ann. At Halloween, Charlie isn’t happy when he sees Bing dressed as Bitey-saurus, but he soon recovers when he realises it is just a bit of fun.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas air a bhith trang a' togail caisteal-sneachd 's iad a-nis a' coimhead air n-adhart ri geama a chluich. 'S e Hari a tha a' lorg am facal an-diugh 's e am broinn an taighe. After building a snow castle in the mountains, the Abadas settle down with Ben for the word game. Soon, Hari is sent to look for a stool inside the house.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha a h-uile duine air an sàrachadh is cùisean cho dòrainneach. Tha Àtaidh a’ togail trèana airson is gun urrainn dhaibh uile a dhol air turas. An uair sin tha beachd aig Tilidh, is tha i a’ moladh gun tèid iad uile air turas timcheall an eilein air fad. ’S e turas air leth a th’ ann, gus an tig rudeigin nan rathad! Everybody is bored. Abney builds a train so they can go on a tour. Then Teal has an idea: why don’t they tour the whole island? It is a fantastic tour until something gets in the way!

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha an t-Iasg-èibhinn ag innse dhuinn gum bi iad a' fuireach air bun-dùn, mar a bhios iad a’ cumail a' bhun-dhùin glan agus mar a bhios am bun-dùn dhan cumail sàbhailte. The Clownfish tells us how they live on sea anemone which they keep clean, and how anemone in turn keep Clownfish safe from predators.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc: Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Rose agus na mialchoin aice, Libby is Marvin. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coin agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Rose is na coin a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh Cormack visits Rose and her beautiful greyhound dogs, Libby and Marvin. We learn how to look after dogs and find out about all the lovely stuff they get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home; including how best to handle, train and feed them.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mairi NicAonghais a’ leughadh Sid nan Sia Dìnnearan. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Inga Moore agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Mairi MacInnes reads Sid nan Sia Dìnnearan, written and illustrated by Inga Moore and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha na Gumbalan uabhasach trang 's iad ri buain na dearc-choille uaine – ach Troig a-mhàin! Chan eil aire-san air na gnothaichean a bha 'n urra ris idir, idir. 'S ann a tha esan a' cur a’ charaidean ann an cunnart! The Gumbals are very busy, harvesting greenberry - except for Troig! He has lost all interest in what he was meant to be doing. In fact, he puts his friends in danger!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha samh grod bho Throig, Bonns is Uilidh nuair a tha iad a' cir geall air a chèile cnuimhean-toilidh ithe - samh cho grod ’s gu bheil an droch fhàileadh a' cur na Bògaisean craicte! There’s a horrible smell from Troig, Bonns and Uilidh when they bet one another to eat chill-grubs - so awful that the smell sends the Bògaisean doolally!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach a' co-dhùnadh gu bheil an t-àm ann fàs fallain - agus tha e ag iarraidh Bitzer a thoirt a-steach air cùisean. Tha beachd eile aig Bitzer ge-tà agus tha e a' tighinn an àrd le plana dìomhair gus an obair chruaidh a sheachnadh. An dèan an sgeama aige a' chùis aig a' cheann thall? The farmer decides it is time to get fit and calls on Bitzer to join him. Bitzer has other ideas and comes up with a secret plan to avoid putting in the hard work. Will his scheme catch up with him in the end?

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Aig Coinneamh nam Pàrant, tha Hilda ag ionnsachadh g’ eil creag bhon Chruinneachadh Nàdair aig Dàibhidh neo-àbhaisteach is, ri linn sin, tha 'd uile ann am fìor chunnart At the parents’ meeting, Hilda learns that one of Daibhidh’s rocks from his nature collection is out of the ordinary. But it puts them all in great danger.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Tha oidhche Shathairne tric a’ ciallachadh ‘takeaway’, ach tha na seòid a’ sealltainn dhuinn gun gabh biadh ‘chippy’ a dhèanamh aig an taigh cuideachd. Tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh iasg blasta le taois-leanna fhad ’s a tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh tiops air am bruich dà thuras. Tha Ùisdean an uairsin a’ dèanamh Scampi agus ‘Clampi” ann an taois tempura le tiops air am bruich trì tursan! Tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh Coleslaw a thèid còmhla ris agus cuideachd sabhs spìosrach. Gus crìoch a chur air a’ phrògram, tha Ùisdean a’ dèanamh donut reòiteig, le Ruairidh a’ dèanamh sabhs caramail airson a ghabhail còmhla ris. Saturday nights often mean takeaway dinners, but the lads show us that excellent 'chippy' food can be made at home, too. Ruaridh cooks a tasty beer-battered fish while Uisdean prepares twice cooked chips to go with it. Uisdean then makes Scampi and 'Clampi' in tempura batter accompanied by thrice-cooked chips! Ruaridh creates a coleslaw and a spicy dipping sauce as an addition. Uisdean then makes an ice cream doughnut while Ruaridh cooks a caramel sauce to go with it. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop is joined by studio guest Ryan Dziadowiec to discuss his interest in farming. Calum Maclean visits an environmental renewal project in Argyll.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc: Griogar MacLeòid a’ dèanamh biadh a-rèir leabhar còcaireachd a sheanmhair. Gregor takes on a classic fruit cake.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc: In the fire, Notre-Dame cathedral lost its light and soul - researchers are working to restore the many things that perished.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: 'S e th' ann am Brot fìor bhlast' de Choiridh leantail, ach lòn sònraicht' nach dìochuimhnich thu ann an cabhaig. An extremely delicious curried lentil soup is a special lunch which you won't forget in a hurry. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: OMC!
programme.desc: Sketch show featuring a collection of comic characters and spoofs. Written by and starring the very best in emerging and established comic talent. Featuring Iain Beggs, Darren Maclean, Carina Macleod, Claire Frances MacNeil, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan and David Walker. Includes the latest updates from the ferry office, a recipe with a difference, and red hot passion finds physical expression via a clown love triangle. Anns an ceithreamh prògram bho shreath ùr OMC! chì sinn tuilleadh sgeidsichean loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail bho na sgriobhadariean is cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann. Gheibh sinn an turas sa beachd car eadar-dhealaichte airson reasabaidh, tha cridhe Doodles an cleasaiche a’ briseadh agus, ’s e cheist as motha an t-seachdan sa, am bidh an aiseig a’ seòladh? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Le ball-coise ann an Alba ann an staing le gainnead chluicheadairean òga a’ faighinn chothroman, tha an SFA airson crathadh a thoirt air na riaghailtean aca. Tha Calum MacIllinnein a’ rannsachadh nam planaichean, a’ coinneachadh ri clubaichean, cluicheadairean is luchd-leantainn, is a’ faighneachd dè thèid again air ionnsachadh bho shiostam Nirribhidh. As Scottish football faces a crisis over its pipeline of talent, the SFA are planning an overhaul of youth development. Calum Maclennan examines the plans, meeting clubs, players and fans, and asks what we can learn from Norway’s system. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Sar Sgeoil
programme.desc: Cathy MacDonald finds out about Frankenstein's Scottish connections. Cathy Dhòmhnallach a’lorg ceanglaichean eadar Frankenstein agus Alba.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona ‘s Otto a' cur romhpa a dhol a choimhead Leum a’ Bhradain ach mus fhaigh iad falbh, feumaidh Otto Pip ‘s Pop a chur dhan leabaidh às-dèidh an t-sealg-oidhch'. Ge-tà, chan eil e coltach g’ eil na cailleachan-oidhche bheaga idir sgìth. Oona and Otto decide to spend the morning watching the 'salmon leap' but before they can set off, Otto must put Pip and Pop to bed after the night hunt. Unfortunately for Otto, it doesnt seem that the young owls are in the least bit tired.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha farspach a’ nochdadh air a’ chreag agus i ann an sunnd airson mi-mhodh. Ge-tà, nuair a dh’fheuchas i ri biadh a ghoid bho fhaoileag bhìodach, tha Oona ‘s Baba a' tighinn na h-aghaidh gus an t-ìsean a dhìon! The great gull has made her way to Puffin Rock and is intent on causing all sorts of mischief. However, when she sets her sights on a poor little seagul chick, Oona and Baba are ready to challenge her and protect the little bird!

programme.desc: Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coin agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Rose is na coin a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc: Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history. Murdo explores Benmore Botanic Garden near Dunoon in Argyll. He visits the Victorian fernery, the Tasmanian Ridge and the Chilean Rainforest Glade where he plants a monkey puzzle tree. Dr Mark Newman of the Royal Botanic Garden, Edinburgh, tells us about the important role of botanic gardens in conservation and education. Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh. Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’gabhail chuairt tro Ghàrradh Luibheanach na Beinne Mòire faisg air Dùn Omhain ann an Earra-Ghaidheal. Tha e a’faicinn a’chruinneachadh rainich, a thòisich san naoitheamh linn deug, agus chì e earrainn den ghàrradh an riochd Tasmania agus cuideachd ceò-choille Chile, far a bheil e fhèin a’cur craobh monkey-puzzle. Carson nach stad an aileag aige? Bheil smachd aig cuideigin air à àiteigin eile? Chan urrainn do Ghriogair sguir a shreothartaich, Lòra a mhèaranaich neo Raghnall a chasadaich. Saoil a bheil iad uile a’ tionndadh nan ròbotan dhà-rìribh? Petit and his friends are having a lot of fun pretending to be robots, until one of them presses a button and Petit gets the hiccups. An uair sin tha beachd aig Tilidh, is tha i a’ moladh gun tèid iad uile air turas timcheall an eilein air fad. ’S e turas air leth a th’ ann, gus an tig rudeigin nan rathad! Everybody is bored. Abney builds a train so they can go on a tour. Then Teal has an idea: why don’t they tour the whole island? It is a fantastic tour until something gets in the way!

Carson nach rachadh an dithis aca-san air saor-làithean mìorbhaileach anns a’ bhothan? Saoil dè cho mìorbhaileach ’s a bhios na saor-làithean aca uile? programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Why are male mandrill faces (big bold primates from West Africa) red and blue? How are birds' feathers so colourful? What do ringtail lemurs do to talk to one another? Their skin holds the key. As Professor Ben Garrod explores how animals communicate with one another, he uncovers a myriad more wonderful ways. Skin has evolved in some remarkable ways to enable animals to communicate with each other, from vibrant displays of colour to skin pouches to amplify sound. Ben shows how animals have evolved to use skin to make themselves heard loud and clear. Birds are notable for their use of coloured feathers to attract mates, show status and as displays of aggression. But, as Ben discovers, long before birds evolved their unrivalled use of colour, it is now believed that their ancestors, the dinosaurs, could well have been using colour to communicate. Ben also uncovers how one species of fish communicates using electricity, and a common British bird has been secretly communicating for years, without us ever knowing.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: In the first of two special walks celebrating the centenary of Dylan Thomas's birth, Derek Brockway walks in Dylan's footsteps around his home town of Swansea. With his guide, actor Adrian Metcalfe, Derek sets off from Dylan's childhood home on Cwmdonkin Drive. He then walks through the city's beautiful parks and down to the seafront before visiting some of Dylan's haunts in later life. Derek even gets to end his walk with a pint! He then heads west to the Llansteffan Peninsula where his guide, artist Osi Rhys Osmond, leads him through the beautiful countryside which was home to many of Dylan's relatives. They visit his aunt's farm, which would provide the inspiration for Dylan's poem Fernhill, before dropping down to the stunning Three Rivers estuary where the Taf, Tywi and Gwendraeth meet.

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: Professor Robert Bartlett explores the impact of the Normans on southern Europe and the Middle East. The Normans spread south in the 11th century, winning control of southern Italy and the island of Sicily. There they created their most prosperous kingdom, where Christianity and Islam co-existed in relative harmony and mutual tolerance. It became a great centre of medieval culture and learning. But events in the Middle East provoked the more aggressive side of the Norman character. In 1095, the Normans enthusiastically answered the pope's call for holy war against Islam and joined the first crusade. They lay siege to Jerusalem and eventually helped win back the holy city from the Muslims. This bloody conquest left a deep rift between Christianity and Islam which is still being felt to this day.

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: In this mind-bending film, Jim Al-Khalili explores the universe at its smallest, from tiny insects to living cells and viruses, before finally arriving at the atom.

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: What is the most toxic animal on earth? How are porcupine quills helping us in medicine? Why is a rhino armour plated, and it is not to protect them from lions? Professor Ben Garrod discovers the complex ways, from camouflage to deadly toxins, in which the skin helps defend animals against threats of all kinds. From the barbed quills of the North American porcupine to the battering ram of a rhino’s horn, the skin has developed an impressive armoury of weapons and warnings to keep predators at bay. With experiments and specialist factual insight, Professor Ben Garrod reveals the toughest and most resilient of animals defend themselves through their skin. One of the most iconic warnings in nature is that of the rattlesnake. Ben takes a teaching sample of a rattlesnake’s tail to the University of Bristol to test just how fast it can vibrate. He uncovers how poison-dart frogs produce their toxins, and how cuttlefish are the masters of disguise when it comes to hiding in plain sight.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: In the second of his two special Dylan's Walks programmes, which celebrate the centenary of Dylan Thomas's birth, Derek Brockway travels to the seaside town of New Quay on Cardigan Bay, where Dylan and his wife Caitlin lived during the war. Derek's hitting the Dylan Thomas trail with his guide Jeff Towns to find out why their time here was so dramatic and how it inspired Dylan to write some of his greatest work. Derek's final walk takes him to Laugharne to visit some iconic Dylan Thomas sites with Hannah Ellis, Dylan and Caitlin's granddaughter. She tells Derek how important Laugharne was to her grandparents and how much it still means to them as a family. Derek ends his walk in great Dylan fashion with a sing-song and a pint at Brown's Hotel.

programme.title: What Are UFOs?
programme.desc: For decades, UFOs have intrigued the world, but many scientists avoided studying them. In the United States, after highly publicised sightings of unidentified objects by US Navy pilots, UFOs are moving out of the shadows and into the light as NASA pledges to study them scientifically. So what does science have to say? Though some are identified as balloons, drones, weather phenomena or optical illusions, others remain mysterious. Could they be the result of secret new technology? And what would it take for alien engineers to traverse vast distances to send probes or visit Earth from other solar systems? Explore the evidence as astrophysicists and engineers use new technologies to investigate the strangest objects in our skies.

programme.title: Television's Opening Night: How the Box Was Born

programme.title: The Fools on the Hill
programme.desc: Dramatisation of the events surrounding the opening night of British television. August 1936, and the BBC prepares for the world's first high-definition TV service. However, behind the scenes at Alexandra Palace complications arise in more ways than one.

programme.title: Television Comes to London
programme.desc: A short film from 1936 that gives viewers an insight into how television came to Alexandra Palace.

programme.title: JLB: The Man Who Saw the Future
programme.desc: In 1926, John Logie Baird became the first man in history to give a successful public demonstration of television. During WWII, with the help of one assistant, a part-time glassblower and a refugee from Germany, he built his masterpiece and swansong - the Telechrome. It was the foundation of all modern electronic colour television. In a lifetime blighted with ill health, JLB - as he was known - produced 178 patents crucial to the technology that would define the 20th century. But since his early death in 1946, his achievements have been allowed to slip from view, obscured by ignorance about what he pioneered. Few are aware that much of his greatest work was done in complete seclusion, in his personal laboratory and entirely at his own expense. Filmed in the UK, USA and Germany between 1994 and 2002 and featuring previously unseen archive and historic eyewitness testimony led by his son Malcolm, this documentary reveals the unknown story of the central figure behind the most powerful technology on earth.

programme.title: The Birth of Television
programme.desc: Leslie Mitchell traces the origins of television, from the beginning of the 20th century to the first outside broadcast - the coronation of George VI in 1937.

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Professor Ben Garrod explores how some snakes can see using heat, how crocodiles feel through their jaws and how some animals use electricity to navigate their world - and it is all only possible because of remarkable adaptations to their skin. Whether animals live on land, in the sea, or in subterranean communities, skin is critical in allowing them to sense the world around them, be it to find food, navigate harsh environments or avoid danger. Even the toughest of animals, crocodilians, have a surprisingly sensitive side when it comes to the specialised skin sensors they use to detect the tiniest of ripples in the water. Deadly pit vipers use heat sensors to ambush the small rodents they feed on. Professor Ben Garrod puts them to the test with an experiment to see if they will strike a cold or warm ping-pong ball. He also uncovers how the less-than-attractive leaf-nosed bat puts its facial skin to good use as an acoustic lens to echolocate around its dense forest habitat.

programme.title: Cornwall's Red River
programme.desc: Poet John Wedgwood Clarke explores the Red River in Cornwall, a watercourse barely more than a stream that has been heavily polluted by centuries of tin mining. Now, this powerful symbol of Cornish identity, home to some very rare, beautiful and resilient species, is slowly showing signs of coming back to life. Extracts from John's poem, Red River at the A30 Culvert, reveal his mixed thoughts about the river's toxic legacy, but as he meets both those with a connection with the river's industrial past and who care for it today, he finds new hope for its future.

programme.desc: Professor Ben Garrod explores how some snakes can see using heat, how crocodiles feel through their jaws and how some animals use electricity to navigate their world - and it is all only possible because of remarkable adaptations to their skin. Whether animals live on land, in the sea, or in subterranean communities, skin is critical in allowing them to sense the world around them, be it to find food, navigate harsh environments or avoid danger. Even the toughest of animals, crocodilians, have a surprisingly sensitive side when it comes to the specialised skin sensors they use to detect the tiniest of ripples in the water. Deadly pit vipers use heat sensors to ambush the small rodents they feed on. Professor Ben Garrod puts them to the test with an experiment to see if they will strike a cold or warm ping-pong ball. He also uncovers how the less-than-attractive leaf-nosed bat puts its facial skin to good use as an acoustic lens to echolocate around its dense forest habitat.

programme.title: Cornwall's Red River
programme.desc: Poet John Wedgwood Clarke explores the Red River in Cornwall, a watercourse barely more than a stream that has been heavily polluted by centuries of tin mining. Now, this powerful symbol of Cornish identity, home to some very rare, beautiful and resilient species, is slowly showing signs of coming back to life. Extracts from John's poem, Red River at the A30 Culvert, reveal his mixed thoughts about the river's toxic legacy, but as he meets both those with a connection with the river's industrial past and who care for it today, he finds new hope for its future.

programme.title: What Are UFOs?
programme.desc: For decades, UFOs have intrigued the world, but many scientists avoided studying them. In the United States, after highly publicised sightings of unidentified objects by US Navy pilots, UFOs are moving out of the shadows and into the light as NASA pledges to study them scientifically. So what does science have to say? Though some are identified as balloons, drones, weather phenomena or optical illusions, others remain mysterious. Could they be the result of secret new technology? And what would it take for alien engineers to traverse vast distances to send probes or visit Earth from other solar systems? Explore the evidence as astrophysicists and engineers use new technologies to investigate the strangest objects in our skies.

programme.title: Mark Lawson Talks To...
programme.desc: Master of horror writing Stephen King talks to Mark Lawson about his book Lisey's Story and discusses the inspiration for his novels and how he battled with his own demons.

programme.title: Singer-Songwriters at the BBC
programme.desc: The celebration of the singing songwriting troubadours of the 1960s and 70s continues with a further trawl through the BBC archives for timeless and classic performances. Don McLean performs his huge hit American Pie from 1972 and Tim Buckley provides some sublime sounds with a rendition of his song Happy Time. Also making an appearance is the long-lamented John Martyn, folk queen Sandy Denny and, in a duet with Joe Egan as Stealers Wheel, the late Gerry Rafferty. Stealers Wheel chum and one-time collaborator Rab Noakes also makes a contribution to this compilation. Leonard Cohen and Julie Felix present a unique collaboration and performance of Hey, That's No Way to Say Goodbye, and there's an unforgettable performance of Case of You by Joni Mitchell. No celebration of this genre would be complete without contributions from songwriting heavyweights such as Elton John, Paul Simon, Loudon Wainwright III and Yusuf Islam aka Cat Stevens.

programme.title: Singer-Songwriters at the BBC
programme.desc: The celebration of the singing songwriting troubadours of the 1960s and 70s continues with a further trawl through the BBC archives for timeless and classic performances. Tom Paxton starts proceedings with a rare black and white performance of his classic song The Last Thing on My Mind filmed in 1964. Also making an appearance is the 'fifth Beatle', Harry Nilsson, with a performance from his BBC concert in 1972. Other gems from this year include Canadian Gordon Lightfoot, songwriting duo Gerry Rafferty and Joe Egan as Stealers Wheel and the most popular acoustic act of the 1970s, the gentle, bespectacled John Denver. From the Basil Brush Show in 1973, Ronnie Lane and Slim Chance make a surprise appearance. Californian Beach Boy Bruce Johnston offers a sublime version of Disney Girls, and Joan Armatrading injects a bit of brio on the Old Grey Whistle Test. Rounding it all off is six-time Grammy winner Billy Joel.

programme.title: US Midterm Elections 26
programme.desc: Live from Washington DC, Clive Myrie, Sumi Somaskanda and Caitríona Perry guide viewers through a decisive night in American politics with far-reaching implications for the world. As polls close and votes pour in across the country, the balance of power in Washington is at stake. Throughout the night, BBC News will bring viewers the latest results as they happen, along with expert analysis of the races, candidates and issues driving voters to the polls, from affordability and immigration to tariffs, international conflict and the growing impact of data centres on local communities. With correspondents reporting from across the United States and the world, plus Ros Atkins at the touchscreen breaking down turnout, voting trends and the shifting balance of power, BBC News will track every major development in real time.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded examines the growing role of artificial intelligence in the US midterm elections. From AI-generated political adverts and deepfake videos to chatbot election advice and algorithm-driven feeds, AI is now embedded in every stage of the information ecosystem. Political campaigns are using AI to create content faster and cheaper than ever before. At the same time, convincing fake videos, synthetic ads and coordinated bot networks are making it harder for voters to separate fact from fiction. With millions of people now turning to chatbots for political information, are we entering an era where AI doesn't just influence elections, but shapes how voters understand them?

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.title: Africa: From Reparations to Action
programme.desc: African Heads of State have gathered at the annual Elevate Africa Presidential Roundtable in Accra, Ghana, to examine how the push for reparations for the transatlantic slave trade can move from recognition and resolutions to meaningful action. In a special Focus on Africa roundtable discussion hosted by Waihiga Mwaura, leaders explore the role of African governments, the African Union, Caribbean partners, and the wider international community in advancing reparative justice. The conversation also looks ahead, asking how Africa can engage its young people in shaping the reparations agenda, strengthen ties with the diaspora, encourage investment and return migration, and create opportunities that support the continent's future development. Bringing together questions of historical accountability and future prosperity, the discussion challenges leaders to move beyond declarations and chart a practical path towards reparative justice and sustainable development.

The United Nations cultural body Unesco has recently given the country's entire cooking tradition special status - that's everything from pasta to pizza, mozzarella to tiramisu. But many Italians have strong opinions about how, when and what to eat, and some unwitting faux pas from visitors can send purists into a frenzy. Briony meets the innovators adding controversial ingredients to pizza and new flavours to ice cream, and the traditionalists who want to keep things exactly as they are.

programme.desc: Roo Irvine treads the boards of Belfast’s Grand Opera House to learn about the architect who put the grand in the theatre’s name! Frank Matcham built some of Britain’s best-known playhouses, and 21 of them are still standing today. Opened in 1895, the Grand Opera House was considered to be Matcham’s crowning glory, and it’s estimated that 35 million visitors have been through its doors since then. In the County Down village of Greyabbey, a curtain raiser of a contest takes place between two teams of in-laws. In blue are Anne Marie and daughter-in-law Jemma. Their high jinks certainly keep Thomas Forrester on his toes. On the other team are Caroline Hawley with Debbie and son-in-law Jacob. They’re ‘red, red ready to win’. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Alison, Sarah Jane, Ciaran and Alan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Packed with new recipes and tips designed to make our busy lives easier, Simply Nigella proves that whatever the occasion, food, in the eating and the making, should always be pleasurable. This episode is all about dishes that marry the comfort of the familiar with the freshness of the new, like Nigella's grown-up take on a family favourite - fluffy oat pancakes with a raspberry and honey syrup. For a fun lunch, there is a riff on the classic caesar salad. A casual supper with friends sees Nigella serving a green-inspired feast of squid and orzo pasta, complete with the Greek dessert of old rag pie - a sweet and savoury twist on a cheesecake. And finally, Nigella's take on a rice bowl with ginger, radish and avocado celebrates a few choice ingredients, resulting in a dish that is calming and uplifting to look at, as well as to eat.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: Tessa MacKenzie studied illustration at university, but it was when she worked in pubs and bars that her fascination with stained glass started. During lockdown, Tessa watched YouTube videos on glass artwork and became obsessed. Completely self-taught, she now works on unique contemporary glass art commissions, from stained-glass window restorations to quirky coasters. We meet Tessa in one of the pubs that first inspired her, and join her in her studio as she creates a unique new glass work, from coloured pen design to soldered and finished lampshade. We see Tessa piece together her glass jigsaw and witness her slightly unorthodox approach to creating stained glass, which includes microwave melting and snapping the glass into shape.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: This Grand Tour follows the River Teviot through Teviotdale, once the haunt of notorious border reivers. In the town of Hawick, Paul Murton joins the annual Common Riding - an event that recalls the border wars with England. In Jedburgh, close to the ruined medieval abbey, Paul is reminded of a crazy night flight by Nazi deputy leader Rudolf Hess. programme.title: The Chief

programme.title: Scotland’s Sacred Islands with Ben Fogle
programme.desc: Ben Fogle explores the ancient sea roads of the Inner Hebrides, with their evocative connections to 6th-century Christian missionaries. On Tiree, Ben explores 1,300-year-old temple ruins. Although remoteness and Viking raids have obscured its history, an undeniable air of spirituality remains. Ben visits crofter Rhoda Meek, who balances farming life with a day job in IT. Julie Clarke left her life in Glasgow to escape a difficult upbringing and moved to the Isle of Coll, transitioning to a woman in the process. The island and its people gave her confidence and support. A highlight of Ben’s journey is a visit to Iona, the island after which he named his daughter. Ben ends his pilgrimage staying overnight in a shepherd's hut.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police uncover a huge cannabis haul in Inverness, search for a missing man in Glencoe, and face a siege after checking on a man believed to be in need of help.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: On the Isle of Skye, fairy tales are more than just stories. From magical pools promising eternal youth, to ancient bridges said to connect our world with the supernatural, the island’s fairy folklore draws thousands of curious visitors every year. But is it all a clever tourist trap, or does something deeper lie behind the legends? In this enchanting adventure, sceptic Zara joins folklore enthusiast Evelyn to investigate the mysteries of Skye’s fairy tradition. At the heart of their journey is Dunvegan Castle’s legendary Fairy Flag, an ancient relic said to have been gifted by a fairy and to hold the power to protect the MacLeod clan in battle. As they uncover dramatic tales of clan warfare, explore Gaelic songs and hear extraordinary stories passed down through generations, Evelyn and Zara discover a tradition woven into the island’s history, identity and culture. Could there be more to the fairies of Skye than meets the eye? And will the promise of eternal youth finally tempt Zara to believe in a little magic?

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Was Mary Queen of Scots responsible for her husband’s murder, or was she the victim of a ruthless plot to destroy her? Evelyn and Zara embark on a royal murder mystery to uncover the truth behind one of Scotland’s most infamous queens. From the shocking death of Lord Darnley to the mysterious Casket Letters, they follow a trail of scandal, suspicion and political intrigue, meeting historians who reveal the secrets behind the story. With affairs, betrayal and power-hungry nobles at every turn, the evidence raises serious questions about who really wanted Darnley dead. Was Mary a murderer, or was she framed by those determined to control her? As her story unfolds, a woman’s fight for power becomes a battle for her reputation, and the legacy she left behind.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: A single mum from Scotland's east coast embarks on a whirlwind romance with a Ghanaian preacher. They quickly marry, and she takes his side as the first lady of his church. But lives are torn apart when tragedy strikes. Reporter Myles Bonnar meets friends and family to try to find out what happened to Charmain.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: Reporter Myles Bonnar travels to Ghana to look into Charmain's death. There, he interrogates the police investigation that was carried out at the time, and meets those who were at the scene, as he searches for the truth about what happened in room 112.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: More than a decade on from her death, reporter Myles Bonnar runs the case by a veteran detective and investigates Eric Adusah's past, uncovering hidden truths. With so many questions about what happened to Charmain, he tracks the Prophet down in search of answers.

programme.title: Growing Up Scottish

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The Traitors continue to wreak havoc on the Faithful at Slane Castle with another brutal murder, but will the Faithful have any luck at the round table? The mission brings the power of the shield back into play.

programme.title: The Hunger Games
programme.desc: As punishment for a failed rebellion, the 12 districts of Panem must offer up two tributes – a boy and a girl to fight to the death in the annual Hunger Games, until only one is left alive.

programme.title: Dating Apps: The Inside Story
programme.desc: Documentary exploring how our love lives have been transformed by the rise of dating apps beginning with Tinder’s explosive launch in 2012. In just over a decade, digital romance has become big business: a global industry worth more than $8 billion, dominated by Match Group, the powerful conglomerate behind 45 platforms, including Tinder, Hinge and OkCupid. With annual revenues around $3.5 billion, Match has reshaped how millions meet, but at what cost? As over half of users report dissatisfaction and Gen Z increasingly turns away from apps in search of genuine, offline connections, the film asks serious questions about safety and the ethics of algorithmic love. Has the pursuit of profit overtaken the pursuit of partnership? Have the platforms been designed to keep us swiping and spending rather than finding 'the one'? Featuring anonymised interviews with industry insiders feeling compelled to speak out, alongside daters, experts and cultural commentators, this documentary uncovers the hidden mechanics of the modern dating economy and asks whether we’ve been seduced, or trapped, by the swipe.

programme.title: OnlyFans: Inside the Machine
programme.desc: Behind the billion-pound success of OnlyFans lies a hidden ecosystem of exploitation. A BBC Current Affairs investigation uncovers allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed by some of the hundreds of agents who manage many of the platform’s creators as well as the potential for modern slavery. Through survivor testimony, undercover access to a managers’ chat forum and expert legal analysis, the film exposes an industry where young women are trapped, threatened and profited from - raising urgent questions about accountability at the heart of one of Britain's most lucrative tech companies.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The New Comedy Awards heads to Middlesbrough, where five hopefuls - Elaine Robertson, Matty Oxley, Vidura Rajapaksa, Chelsea Birkby and Dan Tiernan - battle it out for a place in the grand final in Cardiff. Former New Comedy Awards alumna Lauren Pattison is the host for the evening, and she is joined by stand-up Jonny Pelham and comedian, actress and writer Ria Lina. Keeping the house in order is head judge Fern Brady.

programme.title: The Fast and the Farmer-ish
programme.desc: In the Northern Ireland heat, we meet the Bogmen, three best friends from the heart of Fermanagh, who are up against the Determinators: David, Stephanie and a real life Derry girl, Shannon. Farmer and YouTuber Tom Pemberton hosts as the teams go head-to-head in three high-octane agricultural challenges. The teams are in for a test of raw speed in a drag race and artistic skills in an extraterrestrial mowing challenge. But at least Agnes knows there should not be any problems with the Christmas tree - she is having a very special one delivered...

Chi learns she will only inherit the house on condition she completes a list of 'Things You Should Have Done' left in the parents' will, the first of which is, ironically, learn to drive. Meanwhile, Chi's highly strung auntie Karen wants nothing to do with her dependent pest of a niece, but very much wants the house she feels is rightfully hers. Chi ventures out into Ramsgate in search of a driving license and infiltrates the family of a mild-mannered driving instructor in the process.

Farmer Meinir Howells gets a workout harvesting cockles in Carmarthenshire, and farmer Jim Smith raises a glass to non-alcoholic beer, wine and spirits.

programme.desc: Michael Portillo travels from the medieval city of Stirling through Perth, the historic crowning place of Scottish monarchs, and into Kirkcaldy, where he revisits some fond family memories.

programme.title: Secrets of the Aquarium
programme.desc: Marcus installs a shark cage to allow visitors a close encounter, and a new octopus arrives from Portugal. Amelia has problems that threaten an ambitious project to replant the seagrass meadows.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team are at Lichfield Cathedral in the Midlands. Among the items brought to light is a small statue thought to be from the tomb of Tutankhamun.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today, Flog It! comes from Newby Hall, North Yorkshire. Mark Stacey comes across two unusual tie and stick pins, and Clare Rawle enthuses about a large collection of toy cars. Paul Martin enjoys the Victorian wing of Newby Hall.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Maisie Adam, Ade Edmondson, Rickie Haywood-Williams and Sammi Kinghorn take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is back to give fans the inside scoop and more backstage gossip with this week’s pro panel. And there’s a first look at how the couples are getting on in training.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are back in Norfolk - a bittersweet return, as this was the very first location where Ted joined them. They both reminisce about Ted and raise a cup in his memory - although Ted would have preferred a biscuit. They head to some prime Norfolk lakes, hoping to catch a bream. It’s been well documented that Bob is not a fan of the bream, but will a big catch make him change his tune? It's Paul and Bob's birthday week, and they consider whether they may celebrate any further milestones or simply let them pass. Bob ends up throwing a surprise 70s-themed birthday party for Paul on the roof of the Blickling Estate, once owned by the Boleyn family.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Bioacoustics technology and AI have allowed scientists to not only decode complex animal sound data but also begin communicating with animals. While this may mean the salvation of countless animal species, the advent of inter-species communication could also have far-reaching risks for the ecosystem. In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Hannah takes a look at the vacuum cleaner, going behind the scenes with Dyson and discovering how the motor in their latest vacuum spins nine times faster than that of a Formula One race car. She finds out why a wheezy janitor in the 1900s took inspiration from a sewing machine to create the first popular portable vacuum. And she comes face to face with a colony of creepy crawlies whose job is to help us fight the filth.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team revive a working model of a Welsh coal mine, original plans for a British engineering classic and a Victorian writing box owned by a trailblazing female journalist.

programme.title: Murder in Belfast: Sisters Seeking Justice
programme.desc: Witnesses are in short supply, in spite of the attack beginning in a crowded bar. As public pressure to uncover the killers increases, the IRA tells Robert’s family it has conducted its own investigation and claims to have found out who killed him. But with no-one charged, the search for the truth goes all the way to the White House, where one official sees a way to use the murder to help push the IRA towards going out of business.

programme.title: Ellie & Natasia
programme.desc: Two pregnant mums offer their unfiltered takes on the world of high fashion; eccentric characters take a walk down a very different kind of red carpet; Only Fools and Horses gets an all-female reimagining; a formidable lady claims to have made almost everything that's for sale in the world; a couple's attempt to spice things up in the bedroom goes horribly off the rails; and a serious breakup conversation is interrupted by an agonisingly delayed sneeze. Featuring a guest appearance by Kiell Smith-Bynoe.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: The blame game starts here. Vice-president JD Vance distances himself from his boss, and from last night's crushing election defeat for Republicans. As the Trump era comes to an end, does the infighting begin? Meanwhile the Democrats decide whether to tack to the left or the middle. Victoria Derbyshire asks socialist senator Bernie Sanders.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, explores what the last two years of Donald Trump’s presidency might look like, analyses how the political deadlock in Israel could be broken, and looks at the difficulties and opportunities that artificial intelligence presents to science.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain. As the deadline approaches, Harminder’s father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city. Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities. In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country.

programme.title: The Book That Changed My Life
programme.desc: Inspired by her passion to get people reading, Her Majesty Queen Camilla joins four remarkable people to share the stories of books that shaped them. Warm, emotional and full of hope, the film shows how reading can lift people up, open minds and even change lives in a celebration of the magic power inside every book.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Eva and her Breton guide Tanguy Thomassin explore the vast oyster beds of Cancale, oyster capital of Brittany. Being pummelled by one of the highest tides in Europe makes for fatter, sweeter and healthier oysters. And having once supplied King Louis XVI’s oyster habit, Brittany still supplies half of France. Bretons also boast of plentiful sardines, kelp forests, spiny crabs and the rare cobalt blue lobster. Fished sustainably and cooked on a grill, it's little wonder that this beauty is called the king of lobsters.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: The oil palm is a remarkable tree, with an incredibly diverse fruit that can be used for many different things - from shampoo and soap to toothpaste, crisps and chocolate. Unfortunately, the spread of this remarkable plant is leading to the destruction of the rainforests, particularly in Borneo and Sumatra. So what can we do? Firstly, learn where your food is coming from. Pay attention to the labels and look out for sustainable palm oil. We can’t get rid of palm oil altogether as it is in countless products, and many of the alternatives would be worse. But there are different ways of making palm oil, some of which will not completely destroy the forests. The next thing you could do is buy some forest for yourself. It is possible to fundraise, to get money to purchase a piece of perfect rainforest and protect it. So why not see if you can wash cars, and buy a piece of forest the size of your classroom, the size of your assembly hall, possibly even the size of your school. Finally, think about how you use wood and paper. Make sure you recycle and be sure to think about your impact on the world in every single thing you do. If we don’t, then rainforests could be condemned to history.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: It’s estimated that as many as 250 million sharks are taken from the world’s oceans every single year. Around 73 million of those are taken purely for their fins which are used in shark fin soup, with the rest of the body wasted. This fishing is causing the possibility of extinction for sharks - so, what can we do? First of all, learn about the fish you eat. Fish such as tuna and swordfish are caught with a very high bycatch of shark, which means sharks are caught accidentally when fishing for species. Look for sustainably caught fis, and if in doubt stay clear of it. Be aware of the things that are sold in your local fish and chip shop, as often things that are labelled as huss or rock salmon could actually be shark. And learn to love sharks! Having people understand that sharks are not the menacing, man-eating monsters they are made out to be is so important. Perhaps dream of diving with sharks yourself one day. With our help, sharks can survive into the future.
